synthesis:draft.headline: SA1 peak regional reference price 4981.0 $/MWh at 2026-07-31 02:05 ACST
summary: Peak five-minute regional reference price = 4981.0 $/MWh at 2026-07-31 02:05 ACST (interval ending 2026-07-30T16:35:00Z).
There were 214 five-minute dispatch intervals at or above the analysis threshold of 300.0 $/MWh during the window; mean five-minute RRP over the window = 416.71 $/MWh.
Dispatch TOTALDEMAND at the price peak interval (interval ending 2026-07-30T16:35:00Z) = 1472.82 MW.
Actual operational demand in the half-hour containing the price extreme (half-hour ending 2026-07-30T17:00:00Z) = 1466.0 MW; the window maximum operational demand observed = 2173.0 MW.
Net interchange at the price peak interval = -82.59 MW (negative = net flow into SA1).

possible_explanations.statement: Local reductions in observed unit output (for example, SNAPPER −148.38 MW, AGLHAL −86.79 MW and BLYTHB −70.83 MW) might have tightened supply and contributed to high prices.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Obtain unit outage/availability records, rebid and offer histories, and constraint binding logs for those units and times to determine whether the SCADA drops reflect outages, dispatch down‑orders or bidding/offer changes.

possible_explanations.statement: A planned outage and invoked constraint set affecting the Tailem_Bnd–South_East line (see notice [c2]) might have limited import capability and could have been associated with higher prices.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Retrieve interconnector transfer limit time series and actual flows for the Tailem_Bnd–South_East line and related interconnectors, and check constraint binding reports to see whether S‑TBSE or related constraints were binding during high price intervals.

possible_explanations.statement: An operational disturbance reported by AEMO (City West transformer trip, notice [c1]) might have altered operating conditions and could be related to subsequent price and dispatch outcomes.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Examine secure dispatch instructions, constraint activations and FCAS enablement/activation logs following the non‑credible contingency to see whether operational posture or constraints changed after the event.

possible_explanations.statement: Low WS50M wind speed observations (WS50M wind speed max 3.5 m/s at the Adelaide point) might have reduced wind generation and could have contributed to higher prices.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Compare wind farm generation SCADA traces and availability against the WS50M time series for the window to assess whether reduced wind resource coincided with reduced wind output during high price intervals.

citations.quote: At 1140 hrs, the City West 275/66 kV transformer T_1 and the 275 kV circuit breaker 6675 tripped during restoration of City West 275/66 kV transformer T_2.
citations.supports: reports a non-credible contingency event in the SA region on 30/07/2026

citations.quote: A planned outage of Tailem_Bnd to South_East No 2 275kV LINE in the SA region was scheduled from 1830 hrs 28/07/2026 to 1730 hrs 03/08/2026.
citations.supports: reports a planned interconnector outage and invokes constraint set S-TBSE

uncertainties: Generation changes are SCADA observations; a change in SCADA MW does not by itself show whether it was a forced outage, dispatch instruction or bidding change.
The weather context is a single‑point model product (Adelaide) and not a region‑wide measurement; wind impact should be verified with wind farm SCADA.
Constraint binding records, rebid histories and full interconnector limit time series are not present in the evidence set returned here.
missing_evidence: Time‑series of constraint bindings (which constraints were binding and when) for SA1 during the window.
Interconnector transfer limit histories and detailed flows for all SA interconnectors across the window.
Rebid and offer history and formal outage registration records for units with large SCADA changes (e.g. SNAPPER, AGLHAL, BLYTHB).
FCAS enablement and activation logs and FCAS prices for the window.
